summary: Discovery focused on integration patterns for Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Key concerns: SDK support (LangChain/LlamaIndex), gateway/proxy architecture, rate limits and quotas, observability hooks, security (KMS/SOC2/SSO), and latency/cost tradeoffs. Agreed to SE deep-dive + benchmarks and to share compliance docs and pricing.
transcript:
Header: 2027-10-19 15:00 PDT | Duration: 52m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood SE), Sara (Velox CTO), James (Lead Eng), Anya (Security), Connor (DevOps)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we wanted to cover integration patterns and answer questions about hosted versus dedicated and private options. are there any quick context notes from your side?
[00:08] Sara: yeah thanks, Maya. short context: Velox is an e-commerce platform, we run recommendation and chat assist, mostly on k8s in AWS, some GCP. we're exploring Redwood because of the unit cost and perf claims, and we need VPC/private options for enterprise customers.
[00:20] James: also, we use LangChain heavily in our vector pipelines and LlamaIndex in a few microservices, so SDK support is huge.
[00:30] Diego: great — we do have first-class SDKs, and we've got specific examples for LangChain and LlamaIndex. quick note, some of the bindings in older SDKs had naming diffs so, uh, you might see slight var names, but we provide sample notebooks.
[00:44] Connor: are those samples repo public or do you share per-customer?
[00:48] Priya: we have public quickstarts, and we also send private repos/adjusted samples during POCs. we'll share a LangChain example that shows call-level retries and chunking.
[00:58] Sara: perfect. on auth — we use SAML SSO and we need RBAC across teams. how does Redwood handle that in hosted vs private?
[01:06] Maya: hosted supports SSO and org RBAC; for dedicated/private you get more control — for Private (VPC) you can integrate with your IdP and host the control plane in your network. note: for some older customers we've had to white-label an SSO flow, there's docs we'll share.
[01:24] Anya: and key management? encryption at rest — we need customer-managed keys, HSM or KMS.
[01:30] Diego: we support KMS integrations for Dedicated and Private. for Hosted we have our managed KMS but can support envelope encryption; for enterprise customers we do dedicated key options.
[01:40] [crosstalk]
[01:44] Sara: cool. then on traffic routing — we want to run a gateway/proxy in front of Redwood to enforce per-tenant quotas and mutating headers; is that common?
[01:52] Priya: yes, customers run an edge gateway. Redwood also has a proxying gateway pattern — you can either call our API directly or run a local sidecar/gateway that does rate limiting, caching, and tokenization. some teams put a gateway in their VPC when they use Private.
[02:08] James: does Redwood offer SDK-level rate limit handling? like automatic backoff or client-side throttling?
[02:13] Diego: SDKs include retry/backoff helpers and recommended patterns for batching to reduce RPS. server-side we enforce quotas per API key and per-route. on Dedicated you can configure higher quotas or dedicated throughput limits. small caveat: quotas are soft-limited during bursts unless you opt for reserved capacity.
[02:34] Sara: what's the unit for quotas — tokens or requests?
[02:38] Maya: both — hosted SKU is priced per token and you have request-level rate limits; Dedicated can be provisioned for a certain qps and a token throughput. we'll share the exact quota table in the pricing doc.
[02:51] Connor: we have a requirement to enforce per-customer rate limits inside our app; does Redwood return headers for usage or backlog so we can implement enforcement?
[02:59] Priya: yes we surface rate-limit headers and a usage API; plus we emit metrics to datadog/prometheus when using Dedicated or Private. for Hosted we provide an analytics dashboard and webhooks for alerts.
[03:13] James: observability — we need traceability from our request through Redwood with span IDs, sampling, and log correlation.
[03:19] Diego: we have tracing hooks and recommend OpenTelemetry. Dedicated/Private support OTLP ingestion and you can get token-level latency breakdowns. Hosted exports aggregated telemetry and you can set up event hooks.
[03:33] Anya: what about PII — logs, retention, purge?
[03:36] Maya: by default Hosted keeps short retention, but we offer data retention controls; Dedicated/Private can be configured not to persist prompts or to use customer-managed storage. we'll include our data-retention and deletion SLA in the compliance pack.
[03:51] Sara: good — now on model variants: we want fallback to cheaper models during peak traffic. how do rollouts and automatic fallback work?
[03:59] Diego: smart routing can route based on policy (latency, cost). you can set fallback policies to a cheaper model or quantized variant. Dedicated allows you to pin model versions and create canary traffic rules.
[04:14] James: could we run our own quantized variant in Private and have Redwood route to it?
[04:19] Priya: for Private yes, you can bring your own model bundle and the control plane will handle routing; there's an onboarding step for kernel/quant profiles.
[04:28] [00:04:30] Maya: quick question on latency targets — what's realistic for a 512-token completion in Hosted vs Dedicated?
[04:35] Diego: Hosted median for that profile is ~120-180ms per token tail latencies vary, um median end-to-end might be around 600-900ms depending on prompt complexity; Dedicated with reserved GPUs and optimized kernels can reduce that by ~30-50% for similar load. We'll need to run your prompt set to be precise.
[04:58] James: interesting — what's the pre-warm cost in Dedicated? we can't have cold-starts during promos.
[05:04] Diego: Dedicated has warm pools and can be configured to keep instances hot; there's a cost tradeoff but it avoids cold starts. Also autoscale policies can keep a minimum floor.
[05:16] Sara: we have PCI and EU-data residency constraints — some EU merchants require data never leave region. how does Private help?
[05:24] Maya: Private in your VPC or on-prem addresses that; we support region-restricted control planes and per-tenant data residency. we'll include the deployment topology doc.
[05:35] Anya: audit logs — we need immutable audit trails for admin actions.
[05:40] Priya: we emit admin/audit logs for Dedicated/Private and integrate with SIEM; Hosted has an audit view too but if you need immutable, Private is recommended.
[05:50] Connor: ok thanks. on integration with LangChain: do you provide llm wrappers or caches?
[05:56] Diego: we provide an LLM client that implements the LangChain interface, plus utilities for caching and streaming tokens. note: some older LangChain adapters may have naming mismatches, we include shim adapters.
[06:08] James: and LlamaIndex?
[06:10] Priya: yes, example connectors for LlamaIndex and vector store integrations, and docs for chunking and vector shard strategies.
[06:17] Sara: great. what about websocket streaming? we need partial responses to show typing indicators in UI.
[06:22] Maya: Hosted supports streaming via SSE and websockets; Dedicated/Private support streaming with lower-latency transport. streaming also affects billing model (per-token as they emit).
[06:35] [laughter / filler]
[06:38] James: can you walk through a sample flow if we run a gateway: client -> our gateway -> Redwood API (hosted) vs -> Private within VPC? just quick architecture notes.
[06:47] Diego: sure. if Hosted: gateway does auth/transform, signs request, forwards to Redwood endpoint, receives responses and enforces local per-tenant caching. for Private: gateway sits in your VPC and calls local inference endpoints; you get additional network controls and can keep KMS in your account.
[07:05] Sara: about quotas again — if we exceed tokens do you return a 429 or degrade gracefully?
[07:11] Priya: you get 429s; but we also support soft-limits and a fallback model routing so you can programmatically degrade to a cheaper model instead of hard failing.
[07:23] Anya: are there any compliance or SOC2 nuances for Hosted customers with EU residency?
[07:28] Maya: Hosted can meet SOC2 and we have EU regions; but for strict residency or when customers need full control we recommend Private. we'll attach the SOC2 report and a short note about EU deployments.
[07:42] James: what's the expected onboarding timeline for Dedicated vs Private? we have timelines for Q1 integration.
[07:48] Maya: Dedicated can go live in 4-8 weeks depending on capacity and contract; Private/VPC typically 6-10 weeks including security review and KMS setup. exact timelines depend on your infra readiness.
[07:58] Connor: cost-wise, are there committed options for Dedicated?
[08:01] Maya: yes, reserved capacity contracts monthly/annual to lower unit cost. we'll share pricing table with breakout.
[08:08] Sara: ok for POC — we want to test latency and cost under a sample cart-recommendation workload; we plan to run 10k requests/day and have spike patterns. can Redwood support a short POC?
[08:18] Diego: absolutely. typical POC includes a small reserved pool or hosted trial credits, a prompt set and dataset for benchmarking, and a clear evaluation criteria — latency, token cost, and quality.
[08:30] James: any sample eval harness? we use pytest for perf tests.
[08:33] Priya: we have a perf harness and can share a skeleton that hooks into your pytest or locust. we'll tailor the prompt set.
[08:40] Sara: we'd like to see model regression alerts too; if a new model variant lowers relevance we need to catch it.
[08:46] Diego: Redwood Optimize supports quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to prompt sets — we can enable that for your account during POC.
[08:55] Anya: one last security ask — penetration test evidence and any FedRAMP questions?
[09:00] Maya: we can share pentest summaries and a compliance roadmap. FedRAMP is a longer lift; we don't have FedRAMP yet.
[09:08] [small pause]
[09:12] Maya: okay let's recap next steps — we'll send pricing and TCO, compliance pack (SOC2/ISO), LangChain/LlamaIndex SDK examples, and Diego will set up a benchmark plan. we'll schedule the SE deep-dive for next week.
[09:28] Sara: thanks, that sounds good. any blockers?
[09:31] James: none immediate. we'll confirm internal stakeholders and data residency needs.
[09:36] Maya: great. thanks everyone.
[09:40] [call ends]

Notes: transcript includes occasional transcription noise; some product names appeared as "Redwood Dedicate" in auto-caption, and a couple acronyms mis-spelled (OTEL vs OTLP). Links referenced: (pricing-sheet), (compliance-pack link), (langchain-examples repo).
